subject: Post-call recap: end-to-end p95/p99 acceptance criteria and hosted evaluation
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-health.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: end-to-end p95/p99 acceptance criteria and hosted evaluation

Emma — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks.

High-level ask from Acme Health: confirm that Redwood Hosted API can meet your end-to-end latency targets under production-like load for our patient-facing summarization endpoint. You listed the following acceptance criteria on the call:
- p95 end-to-end (client to client) <= 280 ms for 1–2 concurrent requests per session
- p99 end-to-end <= 480 ms for bursty traffic (peak concurrency up to 30 concurrent user sessions)
- Streaming partial tokens to the client within 120 ms of token generation when streaming is enabled
- Sustained throughput target ~200 TPS for inference across the fleet (with autoscaling)

What we heard about current provider (your notes):
- Current vendor reports API p95 = 330 ms, p99 = 620 ms (attached CSV)
- They use single-model routing, limited streaming buffer, and 5-10s cold-starts for some requests

Our proposed plan (next steps):
1) You share a short anonymized request sample + traffic profile (attached CSV looks helpful) — thanks for sending during the call.
2) Redwood runs a hosted evaluation: two-day PoC that mirrors your traffic profile (regional routing to us-east) and measures end-to-end p95/p99 and streaming latency. We will:
   - Run baseline with your sample (no caching)
   - Run production-like with prefix caching + batching tuned to your distribution
   - Measure p50/p95/p99 and streaming token latency end-to-end (client → Redwood → client)
3) Weekly checkpoint call after day 1; final results + SLA playbook after day 2.

Can you confirm: the target numbers above are accurate and that we can use the anonymized sample you uploaded to the Drive link? Also confirm whether TLS termination happens on your side or if we should assume network hop adds ~20ms.

Attachments: acme-current-provider-latency.csv, acme-slo-requirements.pdf

— Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-health.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Eng Team <eng@acme-health.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: end-to-end p95/p99 acceptance criteria and hosted evaluation

Thanks Vivek — that recap is spot on. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed targets: p95 <= 280ms, p99 <= 480ms (client-to-client) for the summarization endpoint. Streaming partials within 120ms is important for our mobile UX.
- Attached is the anonymized sample and the current-provider export (acme-current-provider-latency.csv). The CSV includes timestamps, downstream client RTT estimates and model token counts.
- TLS: we terminate at our edge; plan for +15-25ms network overhead to your us-east region.
- Cold-starts: we observed 6–9s occasionally during the evening batch jobs; those are problematic for our users.

We are happy to run this as a two-day hosted PoC. The one ask: can Redwood include a streaming-enabled run that uses SSE/websocket so we can validate partial token latency?

Available times for the day-1 checkpoint: Wed 2026-08-05 10:00–11:00 ET or 15:00–16:00 ET.

— Emma
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Health
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-health.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: end-to-end p95/p99 acceptance criteria and hosted evaluation

Looping in a short test plan so we’re aligned internally before kickoff. Vivek / Aditya — proposed test matrix:

1) Baseline run (no caching, single-worker routing)
   - 1m warmup, 15m steady-state at 50 TPS, measure p50/p95/p99
2) Production-like run (prefix/KV cache + continuous batching)
   - Use sample distribution: avg tokens 180, 95th token length 420
   - Run 30m at ramping concurrency up to 200 TPS; measure end-to-end latencies
3) Streaming validation
   - SSE/websocket test with mobile-like client RTT + 100ms jitter, measure first-byte streaming latency and per-token emission latency
4) Stress/peak simulation
   - Burst to emulate 30 concurrent user sessions w/ spikes; verify p99 and request throttling behavior

Instrumentation we will collect: per-request end-to-end RTT, server-side model token timing, queueing wait time, batch sizes, and kernel selection logs. Results packaged in redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx.

Aditya — can you provision a temporary eval config in us-east with streaming enabled and attach the run command + expected metrics collection flags? I’ll schedule the Wed checkpoint once Emma confirms slot.

— Lauren
Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acme-health.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: end-to-end p95/p99 acceptance criteria and hosted evaluation

Emma — thanks for confirming the targets and the sample. I’ve created the eval configuration and a short runbook:
- Eval cluster: redwood-eval-us-east-3 (streaming enabled)
- Config: model=oracle-summarizer-v2, quantization=bf16, autoscale=on, max-burst-concurrency=250
- Run command: redwood eval run --config acme-sla-config.json --duration 2d --traffic-profile drive://acme/sample-profile.json
- Metrics capture: enable --collect=client_rtt,server_model_time,batch_size,kv_cache_hit_rate,stream_first_byte_ms

I also uploaded the initial job manifest and expected dashboards to the Drive folder: https://drive.company/redwood/pocs/acme-sla-checklist (see redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx). Emma — I scheduled the day-1 checkpoint for Wed 2026-08-05 10:00 ET. Invite sent.

Attachments in thread: redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx (test matrix), acme-current-provider-latency.csv, acme-slo-requirements.pdf

— Aditya
SRE, Redwood Inference
